nodes.label: Irrationality of the totient series from one first-harmonic bound on the good indices
nodes.statement: At the minimal admissible depth with s = 26 and η = 1/1000, if for every h ≥ 1 there are arbitrarily large X at which the real part of the first-harmonic sum over the good indices (the assigned indices N in [X, 2X) whose cofactor m satisfies φ(m) ≥ m/1000) is at most 603X/1000, then ∑ φ(n)/2^n is irrational. For all large X more than 67X/100 indices are good, by the unconditional unassigned count and the Chebyshev excluded-cofactor count, and 603/1000 = (9/10)(67/100); the underlying interface asks only for nonempty sets of indices beyond every threshold whose average first cosine is at most 9/10 at a depth with room. The bound is open, sufficient and not known to be necessary. It needs neither the prime number theorem nor a bound on the group means, and it supersedes the prime-number-theorem route at 11X/20. No computation in the record bears on it.

nodes.label: Complex first-harmonic pivot decomposition
nodes.statement: For each positive cofactor m at most sqrt(X)/2, the canonical supplier fibre is exactly the injective image of the primes p in the shifted product interval under N = mp - (L-s+1). This exact bijection does not make a supplier prime globally isolated: at X=16, L=20, s=1, m=2, N=18 the pivot is 38=2*19, while the same prime 19 divides the distinct window argument N+1=19. Removing the pivot phase gives an exact decomposition of the block first-harmonic sum into a centred supplier-fibre correlation, a supplier-fibre mean term, a bad-supplier term, and a non-supplier term. At a positive scale satisfying the explicit dyadic-room inequality, if the real part of the centred term is at most 14X/25 and the other three norms are at most X/100, X/100, and 8X/25, then the real first-harmonic sum is at most 9X/10 and yields a finite certificate. A cofinal supply of these budgets implies irrationality of S. No global supplier-prime isolation, prime-distribution estimate, or decorrelation estimate supplying the budgets is proved.

nodes.label: Fixed-coefficient rewind contraction
nodes.statement: For coefficient c, the canonical inverse parent is T_c(k) = ceil((k+c)/2). For a length-L coefficient list with accumulated offset O, the iterated rewind is R(k) = floor((k+O)/2^L), with phase theta = (1+O) mod 2^L. If 1 <= B <= 2^L, all targets in [1,B] have one ancestor exactly when theta + B - 1 < 2^L; otherwise the endpoint ancestors differ by one and every target maps to one of that adjacent pair. The width bound does not exclude the seam-pair alternative or prove half-membership.

nodes.label: Fixed-precision valuation-unit no-go theorem
nodes.statement: At every fixed positive precision, every finite word of odd valuation-unit symbols admits a compatible carry orbit from an arbitrary incoming integer state, with each successive state within the corresponding valuation-unit radius. Thus bounded local signatures alone cannot exclude all finite centred endpoints; growing precision or global information remains necessary for an endpoint argument.

nodes.label: Fixed-tail survival equivalence at every actual skip
nodes.statement: Writing r_M(1/2) for the residual after ranks through M and T_M for the complete tail after M, an actual skip M is final exactly when T_M < r_M(1/2). Negating the existence of a final skip yields r_M(1/2) <= T_M at every actual skip; together with the no-final-skip classification, this is equivalent to membership of 1/2. The required inequalities along the actual greedy orbit are not proved.

nodes.label: Fresh-prime endpoint-deficit decomposition
nodes.statement: At each positive height, every old-prime endpoint mass dominates the actual totient. The diagonal increment and literal foreign channel split exactly into the old Möbius increment and lower-minus-upper endpoint fresh deficits. The second and five-point curvature operators retain this split, and the nonnegative deficits bound the exact adverse weighted loss from the old-prime curvature margins. nodes.label: Greedy geometry of the Mersenne achievement set
nodes.statement: The Mersenne achievement set is compact, perfect, totally disconnected, nowhere dense, and has Lebesgue measure one. Membership is equivalent to greedy survival at every level; for the target 1/2 it is exactly equivalent to the canonical greedy orbit omitting infinitely many exponents. No finite normalized support has value 1/2, so positive membership would automatically produce an infinite rational-valued support and refute universal #257. Finite exact-rational death certificates soundly prove non-membership (3/4 is excluded at level one). The strict-tail Cantor geometry is recorded by Kovač–Tao; no novelty claim is made for the formalised refinements.

nodes.label: Half-carry reachability and compactness
nodes.statement: At an unresolved even seam, the scalar transition reaches exactly every integer terminal carry other than the one value 2*δ-c. If canonical seam coordinates are supplied at every sufficiently large even depth, then admissible finite half-carry words occur cofinally; compactness yields an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2. The canonical seam-supply hypothesis is not proved.

nodes.label: Finite shadows of the half cylinder
nodes.statement: For an admissible depth-N half-carry word with support A, terminal carry K_N, and future tail T_N, the residual is exactly 1/2 - X_A = (K_N - T_N)/2^N. At a first even seam the sole missing carry is H = 2 delta - c, so the integer strip [1,B] is fully reachable exactly when H lies outside it. The rank-three fixture A = {2,3} has residual 1/42 < 1/32 but its depth-six strip [1,8] contains H = 3, so raw dyadic safety does not force seam escape. The sole conditional membership input is the unproved governed frozen-margin producer, which requires future coefficient rows to cover the centred carry within J <= k+1 after every skipped rank k+1.

nodes.statement: At the doubled feedback row, switching only the terminal half-divisor bit from false to true changes the support coefficient from C to C+1 and, under K' = 2K-C, drops the successor carry by exactly one. The same identity holds for any explicitly identified adjacent boundary pair, and the rewind adapter transfers such a shared-cutoff pair to the next protected seam while retaining the unit-drop witness. nodes.label: Exact band localization of the final skip between two takes
nodes.statement: Suppose a take at rank b is followed by the next take at c > b+1, put q = 2^b − 1 and m = 2^(c−1), and write the pre-take residual as 1/R with 0 < R < q. The final intervening skip is dyadically unsafe exactly when q(m−1)/(q+m−1) < R < qm/(q+m), an interval of exact width q^2/((q+m)(q+m−1)). For one intervening skip this specializes to the two-thirds band (q(2q+1)/(3q+1), 2q(q+1)/(3q+2)), whose width is below 1/9; integral reciprocals never lie there, and the corresponding positive odd numerator is at least 7. These are local constraints: no theorem here says that the actual greedy orbit for 1/2 avoids a band or identifies the surviving last-producer cells with unsafe skips.

nodes.statement: For positive rationally independent clock rates with no simultaneous positive crossings, and integer radices b_i >= 2, all rational relations among 1 and the channel sums S_i are multiples of (-1,b_1-1,...,b_d-1). The proof uses genuine late swaps with a common infinite suffix in one orbit closure, a fixed rational lattice, and density of the clock section. The explicit rates 1,sqrt(2),sqrt(3),sqrt(6) and radices 2,3,5,7 give rational span dimension four. This is an ordinary proof reviewed by AI agents, without Lean or independent human verification of the infinite theorem.

nodes.label: Integer-greedy first-wrap reduction
nodes.statement: For every s >= 3, let C_s = 2^(2s-1) - 2^s, let B_s = 2 floor(sqrt(2s)) + 4, and let r_s be the remainder obtained by greedily subtracting each descending truncated seam weight from C_s whenever possible. Each weight exceeds its complete tail by at least 2^(s+1) > B_s. Hence a positive subset-sum defect at most B_s exists exactly when 1 <= r_s <= B_s. The downstream skipped-seam escape hypothesis requires B_s < r_s at every genuine skipped rank. That hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

nodes.label: Largest skipped-rank gap and successor propagation
nodes.statement: At row s, let d be the largest skipped rank, u the selected prefix below d, L the integer weight of u together with the filled suffix above d, and U the weight obtained by replacing that suffix with d. In the late range d > 2s/3, equivalently 2s < 3d, Lean proves 3L + (3*2^(s+1) + 2*4^(s-d) + 4) = 3U. Upper or middle successors make the new terminal rank s the largest skip, while right successors preserve d. The global statement forcing an upper or middle step when 2(s+1) < 3d first fails is not proved.

Under the hypothesis, induction gives a largest skip beyond two thirds at every row s >= 14; these skipped ranks tend to infinity, so 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set. The window branch chooses carry 1; the seam branch chooses 4 when its unique hole is 3 and 3 otherwise. Either branch supplies one admissible finite word, and the branches may alternate with N. Hence cofinal admissibility and, by compactness, an infinite support A with erdosSupportSeries 2 A = 1/2 follow. This mixed cofinal hypothesis is not proved, so Erdős #257 remains open.

Hence C_(A,d) > Theta_(A,d) iff X_A < 1/2 and C_(A,d) < Theta_(A,d) iff X_A > 1/2; a negative carry is sufficient for the latter because the tail is nonnegative, and carry at most -8 gives a full Mersenne-gap margin. On the non-carry middle branch, failure R' >= 8H is equivalent to the unique cell R = H+k with p^- <= 4k < p^-+4. On the terminal-reset branch, failure is equivalent to R = 3H+k with p^-+4 <= 4k and 4k+16H < 4(R+U)+p^+. These are exact failure classifications, not an avoidance theorem for the concrete seam orbit.

nodes.label: Zudilin rational-base irrationality and irrationality-exponent bound
nodes.statement: For natural numbers 0 < b < a satisfying ZudilinContourRegion a b, the Lambert value F(a/b) is irrational and its irrationality exponent is at most rationalBaseMeasureBound a b. The proof constructs the polynomial forms and proves their clearing, nonvanishing and asymptotic estimates. In particular, F((31/4)^r) is irrational for every positive natural r. These are formalizations of the stated Zudilin region and its consequences, not universal rational-base irrationality; 3/2 is outside the region.
